survey: A classic red phone booth seen in three-quarter view, with the front door facing right of camera and one side panel facing left. The domed roof sits on the box. It has a sign panel and a crown emblem on each visible face, and both line up with the walls below. The front door is a framed glazed panel with a 3×6 grid of glazing bars. Its handle is on the left edge, so it would hinge on the right. The side panel has a matching framed grid of glazing bars. The walls stand fully on a dark rectangular plinth that touches the ground, with no gaps. Inside, a grey payphone is mounted on the back wall and is seen through the door glass, with the glazing bars correctly in front of it. Its handset hangs on the left side of the phone, and a short curled cord runs from the bottom of the phone body. The tools mark no thin parts, ends or branches. Every part attaches where it should. The grid has fewer panes than a real booth and the sign panels are blank. These are simplifications, not errors.
